\begin{example} \end{example}[Newton's law as an Euler--Lagrange equation] ↗ thm:euler-lagrange-equations 1. ch3:3.3.1-ex-1\group Calculus of Variations

For $L(q,x)=\frac12m|q|^2-\phi (x)$, Euler--Lagrange gives \[ m\ddot x=-D\phi (x)=:f(x). \] This is Newton's law (see \cite{FeynmanLeightonSands1966}, Chapter 19). \end{example}

Set $p=D_qL(\dot x,x)$ and assume $p=D_qL(q,x)$ is uniquely solvable as $q=\mathbf q(p,x)$.
